status: REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. The code is not shipped. This records the attempt so it is not repeated.

the_attempt.idea: replace the crit gate's exact-value test (damage == crit_collapsed) with a REACHABILITY test: a damage strictly greater than the maximum possible non-crit roll cannot have come from a non-crit, whatever representative the branch happens to carry. That would cover all three untagged paths in reports/c93 at once -- crit-kill (carries defender HP), crit-survive (carries average_non_kill_crit_damage), and the 16-roll enumeration (carries each roll) -- and would also fix the KO-capped crit the old `damage < pre_hp` guard suppressed, since Showdown does emit |-crit| on a killing crit.
the_attempt.why_it_looked_right: expected_damage_values already computes the raw maxima and discards them for the x0.925 representatives, so the discriminator appeared to be sitting unused in the function. values[0] is max non-crit, values[1] is max crit.
the_attempt.implementation: returned the raw maxima alongside the representatives and gated on max_crit > max_regular && damage > max_regular. Compiled clean; 93 lib tests passed.

measured.baseline: main ca188b93 / e83ee94f era -- diverged 35, matched 15188, skip 1, lossy 11
measured.delta: matched -7, diverged +7, ALL of it in divergence_class:roll_scaled_component (13 -> 20)
measured.both_reconcile: 15224 on both sides, 0 engine errors, so this is a real fidelity regression and not a denominator artifact
measured.verdict: the test tags as crits seven boundaries that Showdown does not tag. It is not conservative; it is wrong in the false-positive direction.

the_cause_of_the_failure.one_line: the raw maxima are only valid at the state where they were computed, and that is not the state the damage is dealt in.
the_cause_of_the_failure.detail: expected_damage_values is called ONCE at render start, from the pre-move state, and it passes Choice::default() for the OTHER side (see its calculate_both_damage_rolls call). The actual damage is dealt after the action phase has run -- after boosts, weather changes, item consumption and the opponent's own move. So max_regular can be lower than the true maximum non-crit damage at the moment of the hit, and any non-crit that exceeds the stale bound is then mislabelled a crit.
the_cause_of_the_failure.why_this_is_the_deeper_problem: the exact-value test and the reachability test fail for the SAME underlying reason: both compare a branch's damage against a quantity computed at a different state. C93 diagnosed the symptom correctly -- the gate cannot see which arm it is looking at -- but the fix it proposed (carry the branch's own roll representative into crit_collapsed) is the only form that avoids this, because it makes the two sides comparable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by recomputation. C77 recorded that form first and it remains the right one.

what_this_costs_and_saves: 7 rows if shipped. Saved by measuring before merging, which is the check PR #1037 failed and PR #1038 made standing: report matched and skip alongside diverged, and require matched to hold or rise.
next: implement C93's disposition as written -- carry the emitting branch's own damage roll into the comparison at the point the branch is rendered, rather than recomputing an expectation from a stale state. That likely means threading a per-branch crit flag or roll index out of generate_instructions rather than inferring crit-ness from values at all, which is what reports/c93 records as the implementable form (instruction.rs carries no crit flag today).
